newsitem.title: USA: Deere Q2 equipment sales rise 15 percent.
newsitem.headline: Deere Q2 equipment sales rise 15 percent.

text.p: Deere & Co said Tuesday its net sales of agricultural, construction and commercial and consumer equipment increased 15 percent to $3.108 billion in the second quarter ended April 30.
Export sales from the United States continued to benefit from increased sales to the former Soviet Union, totaling $547 million for the quarter, up from $415 million a year ago.
Overseas sales also increased, rising by 20 percent over last year's strong second quarter levels, Deere said.
Overall, the company's physical volume of sales (excluding newly consolidated Mexican subsidiaries) increased eight percent for the first six months of 1997, Deere said.

Earlier, Deere reported second quarter income of $319.5 million or $1.25 per share, up from $272.7 million or $1.04 a share. Worldwide net sales and revenues for the second quarter increased 14 percent to $3.521 billion.

"The higher profits resulted from strong worldwide retail demand for the company's products, especially tractors and combines," Deere Chairman Hans Becherer said in a statement. "Operating margins also improved..."

Worldwide agricultural equipment operating profit increased 33 percent to $339 million for the quarter. Worldwide construction equipment operating profit totaled $77 million in the quarter, up from $48 million, Deere said.

Worldwide commercial and consumer equipment operating profit totaled $58 million for the quarter, down from last year's $81 million. The decline was due primarily to higher growth expenditures and costs associated with the discontinuation of the electric start string trimmer line.
Overseas equipment operating profit totaled $112 million for the quarter, up from $101 million a year ago.

The company said its John Deere Capital Corp subsidiary's net income was $29.0 million in the second quarter, down from $37.9 million a year ago. The drop primarily reflected last year's gain from the sale of retail notes.
Net receivables and leases financed by John Deere Capital rose to $6.146 billion at April 30, compared with $4.806 billion a year ago.
